content: In the context of screen-and-treat strategies for cervical cancer, the outcomes of visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) were compared to cytology followed by colposcopic impression. The following outcomes are presented per 1,000,000 patients: 1. Mortality from cervical cancer: VIA with or without cold knife conization (CKC): 144 deaths. VIA with or without loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP): 54 deaths. VIA with or without cryotherapy: 54 deaths. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: 54 deaths. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: 63 deaths. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: 63 deaths. No screening: 250 deaths. 2. Cervical cancer incidence: VIA with or without CKC: 262 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 75 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: 75 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: 76 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: 89 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: 89 cases. No screening: 350 cases. 3. CIN 2+ recurrence: VIA with or without CKC: 3,238 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 2,911 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: 2,911 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: 2,935 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: 3,435 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: 3,435 cases. No screening: 13,400 cases. 4. Undetected CIN 2+ (false negatives): VIA with or without CKC: 5,000 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 4,000 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. No screening: Not applicable. 5. Major bleeding: VIA with or without CKC: 4,901 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 237 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: 36 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: 726 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: 191 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: 29 cases. No screening: 0 cases. 6. Premature delivery: VIA with or without CKC: 5,627 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 545 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: 566 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: 602 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: 536 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: 553 cases. No screening: 500 cases. 7. Infertility: VIA with or without CKC: 6 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: Not applicable. VIA with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. No screening: Not applicable. 8. Major infections: VIA with or without CKC: 793 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 134 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: 14 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: 75 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: 108 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: 11 cases. No screening: 0 cases. 9. Minor infections: VIA with or without CKC: 8,984 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 633 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: 680 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: 792 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: 510 cases. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: 548 cases. No screening: 0 cases. 10. Unnecessarily treated cases (false positives): VIA with or without CKC: 176,000 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 68,000 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. No screening: Not applicable. 11. Cancers detected at first-time screening: VIA with or without CKC: 93,168 cases. VIA with or without LEEP: 47,940 cases. VIA with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without CKC: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without LEEP: Not applicable. Cytology followed by colposcopy with or without cryotherapy: Not applicable. No screening: 0 cases. The data presented above is based on pooled sensitivity and specificity values for VIA and cytology. The sensitivity of VIA is 77% (95% CI: 66–85), and its specificity is 82% (95% CI: 67–91). For cytology (ASCUS), the sensitivity is 84% (95% CI: 76–90), and the specificity is 88% (95% CI: 79–93). Colposcopic impression has a sensitivity of 95% (95% CI: 86–98) but a lower specificity of 42% (95% CI: 26–61). The overall quality of evidence (QoE) for these outcomes is very low due to limitations in the quality of data, indirectness, inconsistency, and imprecision. Assumptions made in the calculations include: No mortality from cervical cancer in true negatives (TN) and false positives (FP). A baseline mortality rate of 250 deaths per 350 women with cervical cancer. A natural persistence rate of 70% for CIN 2+ without treatment, with a 30% regression rate. No major bleeding, infections, or infertility in untreated cases (TN and FN). A 5% population risk of premature delivery in 1% of pregnant women. These findings should primarily be used to compare different screen-and-treat strategies rather than to assess outcomes within specific age groups.
